thread:
support-anna: FYI customer running Redwood Private across eu-west-1 and us-east-1 reporting intermittent 503s & TLS errors when calling our private API from their app in us-east-1. They say eu-west resolves to internal ALB but us-east resolves to a public proxy IP. Can infra help triage?

customer-tech: Repro steps from our side: every ~10 mins calls to https://private-api.redwood.internal return 503 then 200. We ran nslookup from two EC2s (one in each region):
```
# eu-west-1
$ dig +short private-api.redwood.internal
10.2.5.12

# us-east-1
$ dig +short private-api.redwood.internal
54.210.33.44
```
We also see TLS error in app logs: "tls: certificate is valid for redwood-internal.local, not private-api.redwood.internal"

jamal_k: Thanks, that's super helpful. Two immediate suspects: 1) split-horizon/private hosted zone not associated with the us-east VPC (so public DNS answer leaks in), or 2) something on the egress path rewriting DNS (corporate FW / NAT / resolver). Can you paste output of `dig +trace private-api.redwood.internal` and `tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 53` from the us-east instance?

customer-tech: Pasting trace + tcpdump snippets below (sanitized):
```
; dig +trace
; ->  . (root)
;; Received 512 bytes
;; global options: +cmd
private-api.redwood.internal. 60 IN A 54.210.33.44

# tcpdump: (us-east)
13:12:33.123456 IP 10.0.2.10.12345 > 172.16.0.10.53: 1234+ A? private-api.redwood.internal. (40)
13:12:33.123789 IP 172.16.0.10.53 > 10.0.2.10.12345: 1234* 1/0/0 A 54.210.33.44 (56)
```

alex_w: The TCP dump shows DNS replies from 172.16.0.10 (their resolver). Is that their on-prem forwarder or a cloud FW? If their on-prem forwarder uses a cached public answer we could get the public IP. Also the TLS CN mismatch implies the public IP is serving a cert for a different CN.

maria_s: Quick checklist: 1) Confirm Route53 private hosted zone exists for redwood.internal 2) Confirm VPC association in both regions (aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z1234 and list-associations) 3) Check any conditional forwarders / resolver endpoints (Route53 Resolver endpoints) 4) Verify egress allowlist / firewall is not forcing DNS to 8.8.8.8 or a corporate resolver that lacks the private zone.

customer-tech: Running the AWS checks now. One odd bit: the hosted zone is associated to VPC vpc-0a1b2c (eu-west) and vpc-0d2e3f (us-east) according to console, but the us-east service team says they created a split-horizon proxy (transparent forwarder) to 172.16.0.10 for all DNS. The proxy will return public answers unless the zone is on their resolver.

support-anna: That explains the mixed answers. Two things to validate from our side: 1) Whether the private ALB/ENI IP (10.2.5.12) is reachable from us-east (security groups, NACLs, routing). 2) Whether our internal TLS cert is provisioned for the hostname that the app uses. Could the app be using SNI `private-api.redwood.internal` but getting connection to the public proxy which presents a different cert?

jamal_k: Can you run `curl -v --resolve private-api.redwood.internal:443:54.210.33.44 https://private-api.redwood.internal/health` from us-east and paste the TLS handshake output? Also run `curl -v --resolve private-api.redwood.internal:443:10.2.5.12 https://private-api.redwood.internal/health` from eu-west for comparison.

customer-tech: Outputs:
```
# us-east -> public IP
* Connected to 54.210.33.44 (54.210.33.44) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: Server certificate: CN=redwood-public.proxy
* SSL: certificate subject name (redwood-public.proxy) does not match target host name 'private-api.redwood.internal'
* Closing connection 0

# eu-west -> internal IP
* Connected to 10.2.5.12 (10.2.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: Server certificate: CN=private-api.redwood.internal
* HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

alex_w: So root cause is DNS in us-east resolving to a public proxy IP that isn't presenting our internal cert and is returning 503s intermittently. Fix paths: a) update their forwarder so it resolves the private hosted zone (or stop forwarding and use AmazonProvidedDNS in-VPC), or b) ensure their proxy forwards queries to the Route53 resolver via an outbound Resolver endpoint with proper VPC association, or c) associate the private hosted zone to the VPC that actually answers DNS requests.

maria_s: Also advise them to lower client-side DNS TTL temporarily and flush DNS caches (both on app instances and on any proxy) after changes so the stale public record doesn't persist. If their proxy mixes answers based on its own cache, that would explain the intermittent pattern.

customer-tech: We updated the proxy to forward queries to the regional Route53 resolver IPs (VPC CIDR + .2 .3 addresses) and explicitly allowed UDP/TCP 53 to those endpoints in the firewall. After flushing caches and waiting ~90s, we see consistent internal IPs now and TLS errors disappeared.

support-anna: Nice. Two follow-ups for internal docs: 1) Add checklist for customers running split-forwarders that includes Route53 Resolver endpoint targets and common firewall ports (UDP/TCP 53, allowlist route53 resolver IPs, NTP if used for cert validity). 2) Add recommended low TTL during migration and note that transparent proxies can create split-horizon inconsistencies. I'll file a quick KB.

ops-bot: Ticket #INC-2026-981 created and linked to customer account.

jamal_k: TL;DR for support notes: intermittent 503/TLS CN mismatch due to region-specific DNS forwarder returning public IPs. Root cause: forwarder cache + missing forwarding to Route53 resolver. Resolution: point forwarder to Route53 resolver OR use VPC AmazonProvidedDNS; open UDP/TCP 53 to resolver IPs; flush caches; verify cert CN. :white_check_mark:

customer-tech: Thanks all, will keep monitoring. :pray:
